title: dedicated-autoscaler: add burst throttle, throughput guarantees, and per-fleet utilization reporting
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: customers running Dedicated capacity reported tail latency spikes during short bursts and lack of per-fleet utilization visibility. This PR introduces a token-bucket burst throttle and soft-queueing policy at the fleet level, explicit throughput guarantees for reserved pools, and a new per-fleet utilization reporting endpoint consumed by the Console. Changes include runtime throttling logic, allocator adjustments, metrics export, API proto extensions, chart defaults, and E2E tests. Checklist: - [x] Implement token-bucket burst throttle and soft queueing - [x] Add throughput guarantee config and enforcement in allocator - [x] Export per-fleet utilization and burst metrics (tokens, queue depth, throttled requests) - [x] Add API proto and server handler for utilization reporting - [x] Add e2e tests simulating burst traffic and guarantee violations - [x] Update helm chart and docs - [x] Run perf benchmarks and CI. Related: Linear ENG-4821 (autoscaler burst controls), ENG-4910 (fleet utilization reporting). Notes on behavior: throttle is conservative by default and can be overridden per-fleet via DedicatedConfig.burst: {burst_capacity, refill_rate, soft_queue_ms}. Throughput guarantees are expressed as requests-per-second committed to a reserved pool and enforced by the allocator with a best-effort fallback to compatible fleets when guarantees cannot be met. Observability: new metrics exported under redwood.autoscaler.fleet.* and a /api/v1/fleets/{id}/utilization endpoint returns the last 5m utilization window. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated for 48h then enable by default for GA. If we see queue buildup > 99th percentile or dropped tokens > 1% across fleets, revert the flag and roll back the allocator change. Test plan: unit tests added for token-bucket, allocator integration tests, e2e load test reproducing earlier incident. Backwards compatibility: proto additions are additive; clients that don't read the utilization endpoint are unaffected. Documentation: updated docs/observability/dedicated-autoscaler.md and helm values.
commits: Enforce throughput guarantees in allocator and add fallback routing (services/autoscaler/allocator.go)
Expose per-fleet metrics and reporting API (pkg/metrics/fleet_metrics.go, api/v1/fleet_handler.go)
review_comments: Ethan Chen: Left a few inline nits but overall LGTM. Question on whether soft_queue_ms should be per-request or per-fleet. Please justify and add a comment.
Ava Patel: Responded - soft_queue_ms is per-fleet because queueing on a per-request basis created head-of-line issues; added comment and test that verifies queue behavior under mixed priorities.
Lina Gomez: Noted potential metric cardinality growth; request to aggregate label set to (fleet_id, region) only. Ava updated metrics export to limit labels.
Miguel Torres: Observability look OK; requested one more e2e run against a larger fleet config. Ran overnight and attached perf numbers in CI.
Ethan Chen: Approved after comments addressed and CI green.
release_notes: Added fleet-level burst token-bucket throttle and soft-queueing to reduce tail latency during short bursts
Introduced throughput guarantees for reserved pools with best-effort fallback routing
Added per-fleet utilization reporting endpoint and new autoscaler metrics for Console integration
notes: Feature gated behind dedicated.autoscaler.experimental=true for 48h rollout
Config knobs added to DedicatedConfig.burst: burst_capacity, refill_rate, soft_queue_ms
